title: per-request-quant-switching-cost-model-sheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This sheet prototypes a cost/latency model for per-request quantization switching (runtime selecting a higher- or lower-precision variant on a per-request basis). Goal is to capture the tradeoffs between token unit cost, end-to-end latency (including switch overhead), and quality delta for typical Redwood workloads (chat short-turns, long generation, embedding-heavy queries).

Key definitions (plain language):
- ModelVariant: a deployed binary of the same base model compiled/quantized to a given precision (e.g., FP8, INT8, 4-bit).
- Switch overhead: the additional latency and potential cost when one request is routed to a different variant than the previous request on the same worker (warmup, KV cache rehydrate, context transfer). Expressed as milliseconds and as extra token-equivalents for cost amortization.
- Effective token cost: operator-visible cost per output token after accounting for batching efficiency, GPU occupancy delta across variants, and amortized switch overhead.
- Quality penalty: measured degradation in downstream metric (e.g., ROUGE, BLEU, human rating) relative to high-precision baseline. Represented as a normalized score where 0.0 = baseline quality.

Sheet layout (tab names and columns):
1) SUMMARY_TAB (one-line cells and computed outputs)
- Workload profile: typical tokens per request, prefix hit rate (%), fraction of short-turns (<64 tokens), fraction of long-turns (>512 tokens)
- Latency SLO target (ms)
- Decision rule summary (e.g., switch-to-low if expected tokens<X AND latency budget <Y)
- Summary outputs: estimated monthly cost delta, % requests switched, projected quality regression

2) VARIANTS (row per variant)
Columns: variant_id, precision (4-bit|INT8|FP8|FP16), peak_throughput_tok_s, avg_latency_token_ms, token_unit_cost_usd, avg_batch_size, kv_hit_efficiency (0-1), notes
Sample rows: 
- v_fp16, FP16, 350k tok/s, 0.9ms/token, 0.0020 USD/1k tokens, batch 16, kv 0.95
- v_fp8, FP8, 420k tok/s, 0.78ms/token, 0.0014 USD/1k tokens, batch 20, kv 0.92
- v_int8, INT8, 500k tok/s, 0.65ms/token, 0.0011 USD/1k tokens, batch 24, kv 0.88
- v_4bit, 4-bit, 680k tok/s, 0.48ms/token, 0.0008 USD/1k tokens, batch 28, kv 0.8

3) SWITCH_OVERHEADS (matrix + per-worker amortization)
Columns: from_variant, to_variant, cold_switch_ms, warm_switch_ms, amortize_tokens_equiv
Notes: cold_switch covers loading weights / reinitializing kernels. warm_switch covers KV rehydrate and scheduling jitter. amortize_tokens_equiv maps ms -> equivalent token cost on destination variant (ms / avg_latency_token_ms).
Example: from v_fp16 to v_4bit: cold_switch_ms=4200, warm_switch_ms=45, amortize_tokens_equiv=900

4) WORKLOAD_SEGMENTS (user-defined segments)
Columns: segment_id, pct_requests, avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens, quality_sensitivity (high|medium|low), preferred_latency_budget_ms
Sample: chat_short, 0.62, 18, 24, high, 150ms
chat_long, 0.08, 1200, 900, medium, 1200ms
embedding, 0.12, 4, 0, low, 100ms

5) DECISION_SIM (per-segment simulation outputs)
Columns: segment_id, chosen_variant, pct_switched, avg_end_to_end_ms, effective_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, projected_quality_delta
Description of simulation logic (simple deterministic rule engine for the prototype):
- For each segment compute expected end-to-end latency if served entirely by each variant: E2E_ms = avg_input_tokens*encode_ms + avg_output_tokens*variant.avg_latency_token_ms + expected_switch_overhead_ms (if the route requires switching; model estimates switch probability from prefix cache and worker affinity).
- Compute effective cost per 1k tokens: base_token_cost * (1 + batching_efficiency_factor) + (amortized_switch_tokens/1000) * token_unit_cost_of_chosen_variant. Batching efficiency factor is negative when larger batches reduce per-token cost; for prototype use 1 / avg_batch_size as proxy.
- Add a quality penalty score if using lower precision: quality_delta = measured_score_low - baseline_score_fp16 (negative means regression). Use per-variant quality offsets provided in VARIANTS notes.
- Decision rule picks the cheapest variant that meets the latency SLO and has allowable quality delta threshold. If none meets latency, fallback to next best latency variant (configurable).

6) OUTPUTS & EXAMPLES (auto-calculated textual recommendations)
- Example result for chat_short: recommends v_int8 for 72% of requests, fallback v_fp8 for 18%, v_fp16 for 10% for quality-critical prompts. Estimated monthly savings: $12,300 vs FP16 baseline, projected overall quality delta: -0.8% on human rating.
- Example result for embedding segment: recommend v_4bit always (cost savings 68%), latency within SLO, quality delta negligible.
- Example overall policy: "Switch-to-lower-precision when expected output tokens < 128 AND predicted quality-sensitivity == low OR (predicted quality-sensitivity == medium AND delta_quality_loss < 1%)"

Heuristic knobs to expose (for product integration):
- SwitchProbabilityBias: adjust conservativeness of switching to avoid thrash when worker affinity low
- MinTokensToSwitch: do not switch for requests with expected tokens < X to avoid amortization overhead
- QualitySlackPct: allowed quality degradation per segment before forcing high-precision
- LatencyBufferPct: fraction of SLO reserved for switching overhead and tail latency

Open questions & data needs (next steps):
- Need microbench matrix for all model/precision pairs including cold load times across all hardware SKUs (A100, H100, L40x). Current numbers are placeholders.
- Measure real-world prefix cache hit correlation with request ordering; needed to estimate switch probability per worker.
- Run A/B on live traffic with conservative Split (5%) to validate quality deltas and switch overhead assumptions.
- Investigate whether KV caching across variants (shared KV store) can reduce the warm_switch_ms measurably; if so, amortization model changes.

Implementation notes for runtime: 
- Runtime needs per-worker lightweight affinity tracking (last_variant_served, last_request_time) to estimate switch overhead probabilities without centralized coordination.
- Add metric emission: switch_count, switch_type(cold|warm), avg_switch_latency_ms, per-segment_quality_metric to feed Optimize quality monitoring.

Appendix A: sample formulas (human-readable)
- amortized_switch_token_equiv = switch_ms / variant.avg_latency_token_ms
- effective_cost_per_1k = variant.token_unit_cost_usd + (amortized_switch_token_equiv / 1000) * variant.token_unit_cost_usd + (base_overhead_fee_usd_per_request * 1000 / avg_output_tokens)
- avg_end_to_end_ms = network_ms + encode_ms + (avg_output_tokens * variant.avg_latency_token_ms) + expected_warm_switch_ms

Appendix B: quick sensitivity table (to be expanded into real sheet columns)
- Varying SwitchProbability (0%, 10%, 30%, 60%) vs cost savings and quality tradeoff for chat_short segment.

TODO checklist:

- [ ] Add actual baseline quality deltas per dataset (action: applied-ml)
- [ ] Wire sheet to simulation harness or quick Python script for Monte Carlo sensitivity tests (action: product-optimize / eng)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and favors a simple deterministic decision rule for initial experiments. We can iterate to probabilistic policies or RL-based policies later, but first objective is to prove unit-economics and safety (quality preserved).
